decisions.quote:
Childers and Tomasello (2001) found that training 2 1/2 -year-olds on the English transitive construction greatly improves their
                        performance on a post-test in which they must use novel verbs in that construction. In the current study, we replicated Childers
                        and Tomasello’s finding, but using a much lower frequency of transitive verbs and models in training. We also used novel verbs
                        that were of a different semantic class to our training verbs, demonstrating that semantic homogeneity is not crucial for gener-
                        alization. We also replicated the finding that 4-year-olds are significantly more productive than 2 1/2 -year-olds with the transitive
                        construction, with the new finding that this is also true for verbs of emission.

The abstract expressly says it also replicated greater transitive productivity at4than2.5years. Novel emission-verb content does not by itself erase the broader actual age comparison; conversely a review is not itself an empirical original and a general claim does not prove a separate missingpaper. initial_expert_decision.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work. The blind coder created an unidentified target (target_index 1, with empty authors, year, title, and doi) for the statement that 4-year-olds are significantly more productive than 2.5-year-olds with the transitive construction. Full-text inspection of 7bc9ff8a5446a5aa.txt positively establishes that this age comparison is not a replication of a distinct, uncaptured primary empirical study: (1) In the Introduction (lines 48-50, left column), the authors explicitly state that 'The only transitive construction training study with pre-schoolers in which productivity was tested with novel verbs is that of Childers and Tomasello (2001)', which is already captured in shipped row input_row_index 2341 (Childers & Tomasello, 2001, 'The role of pronouns in young children's acquisition of the English transitive construction.', DOI 10.1037/0012-1649.37.6.739, matching target_index 0). (2) The general developmental benchmark that 4-year-olds are more productive with the transitive construction than 2-year-olds is attributed in the Introduction (lines 38-47, left column) to 'A number of studies' and cited solely to a review article ('see Tomasello, 2000, for a review' — Tomasello, 2000, Cognition, 74, 209-253, 'Do young children have adult syntactic competence?'), and again in the Discussion (lines 340-343, left column) to '(e.g. Tomasello, 2000)'. Under the codebook, a review article or general multi-study phenomenon is not an eligible primary original target. (3) Furthermore, the Introduction (lines 104-107, right column) states that testing 4-year-olds on novel verbs of emission was included as a novel extension ('we also checked that 4-year-olds are productive with the transitive construction with novel verbs of emission, as this had never previously been reported in the literature').
